title: Build your crew tag filter
copy: Crew and family tags rarely overlap, so put alternatives in one group and stack a second group when you want both to be true.

formula.empty: every character — no tag groups yet

selection.locked: This page always requires every group to match.

announced.all: Every group must now match. {{count}} characters match.
announced.any: Any group may now match. {{count}} characters match.

sets.title: Your tag groups
sets.maxReached: You can build up to {{max}} groups.
sets.overCap: This filter already has {{count}} groups, more than the {{max}} you can add here. Existing groups are kept so your results do not change.
sets.emptyIgnored: This group is empty, so it is ignored.
sets.nullifying: No character carries every tag in this group, so nothing can match. Most crews and families do not overlap — try switching this group to "Is any of these".

announced.any: Group {{index}} now matches any of its tags. {{count}} characters match.
announced.anyNoCount: Group {{index}} now matches any of its tags.
announced.all: Group {{index}} now requires all of its tags. {{count}} characters match.
announced.allNoCount: Group {{index}} now requires all of its tags.

explainer.title: Two ways a group can match
explainer.anyCopy: A character needs at least one tag from the group. This is the usual choice, because a character is rarely in two crews at once.
explainer.allCopy: A character must carry every tag in the group. Useful for tags that stack, like a crew plus an arc — but it finds nobody when the tags exclude each other.
explainer.sample: Example: a group with "Straw Hat Pirates or Heart Pirates", plus a second group with "Dressrosa", finds characters from either crew who also appear in Dressrosa.
